_comment: Carry destination for the mutation-survivor class fix (#1412) -- the
un-landed POPULATOR half. This PR lands the enforcement half (the
deterministic inventory, the completeness ledger, the unpinned-site
ratchet and the cap_problems refusal in tests/mutation_table.py); the
nightly burn-in that populates the `killed_by` ledger (the RCA's
populator, a run-id-derived seed that censuses the pool and refuses a
census that fails to grow) is a follow-up stage with no roster group,
so this file is that stage's brief. Shape and required fields:
stage: any later seat that implements the nightly burn-in which populates the `killed_by` ledger in tests/mutation_budgets.json -- the RCA's populator (a run-id-derived seed over the deterministic inventory, recording each killed mutant's driver and refusing a census that fails to grow)

carries.from: the pull request that adds inventory(), the completeness ledger and the unpinned-site ratchet to tests/mutation_table.py (the enforcement half of #1412; the populator half is not landed by it)
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. Enumerating all 3798 candidates over 64 production modules through `mutation_table.inventory()` and grouping by the ledger key `triage_key(s)` = `file:line KIND` yields 46 keys with two candidates each, and every one of the 46 is CLAMP_DROP -- a line carrying two `min`/`max` calls, whose two candidates share the same `old` (the whole line text) but differ in `new` (which call is replaced). The null control is the other five operators: the same census over GUARD_OFF (2012), RETURN_DEL (902), BOOLOP (315), CONST (133) and RAISE_DEL (4) yields zero keys with more than one candidate, so the collision is specific to CLAMP_DROP's per-call generation, not a general property of the key. The perturbation that would void the finding is keying on `(file, line, kind, new)` instead of `(file, line, kind)`: that census finds zero collisions, because the `new` text disambiguates the inner call from the outer call. The concrete instance is custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py:4671, `p_dhw_run = max(0.1, min(p_max * 0.8, p_max))`: two CLAMP_DROP candidates share the key and the same `old`, so a single disposition at that key covers both and cannot say the inner `min` is a dead clamp (equivalent) while the outer `max` is a real clamp -- which is exactly why that dead-clamp instance is not recorded under survivor_triage in this PR.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this paragraph's count: it is measured at this PR's head, and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. Re-run `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tests'); import mutation_table as m; from collections import Counter; c=Counter(m.triage_key(s) for s in m.inventory()); print(sorted((k,v) for k,v in c.items() if v>1))"` from the repository root and read the printed keys: expect exactly the colliding CLAMP_DROP lines, and confirm the other five kinds contribute none. Then perturb: key the same census on `(file, line, kind, new)` and confirm the collisions disappear. A populator that records a disposition for a colliding line without accounting for both candidates silently marks a real clamp equivalent to a void one.
carries.brief: The ledger key `file:line KIND` plus the `old` pin does not uniquely identify a candidate site where a line carries two `min`/`max` calls: 46 such lines exist, all CLAMP_DROP, each yielding two candidates with the same key and `old` but a different mutation. The populator that fills `killed_by` in tests/mutation_budgets.json must therefore key on the mutation target -- the text it replaces, or the source segment -- not on `file:line KIND` alone, before it writes a disposition for a colliding line; a disposition keyed only on the line covers both candidates and cannot express that one is void (a dead clamp) while the other is a real clamp. The instance that made this concrete is a dead inner clamp inside a real outer clamp on the same line, left unrecorded in this PR for exactly that reason.

carries.from: the pull request that closes #1453 (D3-02): tests/mutation_table.py's kill rule moved into `killed()`, which reads a status a driver declares in NON_VIOLATION_EXITS (tests/structure.py's exit 2, IMPROVED AND NOT YET RECORDED) as 0 while the output names no FAIL line
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. Over the round-7 D3 finder's frozen sample (tools/audit/round7/D3/sample.json at f9d6f782), re-anchored by line text to cdf82daa (36 of 40 kept), tests/structure.py fired on 3 mutants in both trees; the merge base's inline rule recorded all 3 as killed, one of them (coordinator.py GUARD_OFF in cut_learning's call graph, rc 2, zero FAIL lines, cut_learning 285 -> 284) with no failing check; `killed()` records the two rc-1 BREACHED fires as kills and that one as not killed. Null control: the unmutated tree against itself is not a kill in either tree, and rc 2 printed beside a FAIL line was a kill. That check is now tests/entities.py's `a status is a kill for no driver unless the output names a failing check`, which, since #1521, reads rc 2 with no failing check as no kill from EVERY driver (the per-driver key this entry measured is retired) and still reads rc 2 beside a FAIL line as a kill.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust these counts: they are measured at that PR's head, and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. Re-read `killed()` and `failing_count()` in tests/mutation_table.py (the #1521 carry below retired `NON_VIOLATION_EXITS`), and confirm tests/structure.py's `ratchet()` still returns 2 only on the unrecorded-improvement path (the three `_MUT_S_*` checks in tests/entities.py drive it).
carries.brief: The populator that records `killed_by` must take its verdict from tests/mutation_table.py's `killed(script, run, baseline)`, never from its own comparison of exit statuses: a status is not a failed check, and tests/structure.py exits 2 for a metric that only IMPROVED -- a mutant that makes code unreachable can do that -- so a populator keyed on `rc != baseline.rc` would write `killed_by: tests/structure.py` for a site no check covers and take it off the unpinned count. Superseded in part by the #1521 carry below: the per-driver NON_VIOLATION_EXITS table is retired, and no driver's status is a kill on its own.

carries.from: the pull request that closes #1521 (R8-D3-s1-01): tests/mutation_table.py's `killed(script, run, baseline)` counts a kill only on a red run that names more failing checks than the unmutated baseline (`failing_count`), and every run drives a comment-only null control (`null_control`) through every driver in play, refusing itself (`null_control_refusal`) when it does not survive
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. While the fork point carries a claim list the diff leaves alone (tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt carries one solver line at 0011bc73), tests/env_drift.py refuses every production edit with INHERITED CLAIMS before capturing anything; the finder's harness (round-8 transport commit 6f58e33, handoff/round8/evidence/D3/s1_claimkill.py) counts 17 of 17 mutants refused, the comment-only edit included, and 0 with the claim list emptied (its perturbation). Scored by each tree's own kill rule against the unmutated run, the merge base's rule records those refusals as kills and this pull request's records none; the null control is the unmutated run scored against itself, which neither rule calls a kill. tests/entities.py drives the real refusal texts (`inherited_claims_error`, `record_pr_claims_error`, `self_comparison_error`) through `killed()` as no kill, and a drift verdict and a stale fixture as kills. An uncaught exception on a red run is a kill whatever its class: the first cut keyed it on the exception line's class name and scored 7 real traceback shapes as no kill (UpdateFailed, AbortFlow, ConfigEntryNotReady, ProcessWorkerUnavailable, StopIteration, a multi-line assert, an exception with notes -- #1561's review, 9 of 9 kills at its merge base against 2 of 9); the rule now keys on the traceback header and rc != 0, driven by tests/entities.py's `any uncaught exception on a red run is a kill, whatever its class` over real subprocess tracebacks, with a traceback-free exit 1 as its null control.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust the counts: they are measured at that pull request's head and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. Re-read `killed()`, `failing_count()` and `null_control()` in tests/mutation_table.py, and check whether tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt carries a line at your merge base: while it does, tests/env_drift.py judges no mutant at all (it refuses before capturing), so a site only env_drift.py could reach is an honest survivor there, not a kill.
carries.brief: The populator that records `killed_by` must take each verdict from `killed()` in a run whose null control survived, and must never record `killed_by: tests/env_drift.py` from a run in which env_drift.py refused before capturing (INHERITED CLAIMS, RECORD PR CLAIMS, SELF-COMPARISON): a refusal judges the diff's claim files, not the mutated line. A driver that prints a failing-check form `failing_count()` does not read is extended there, and tests/mutation_table.py's `main()` refuses a run whose drivers include one whose source prints none (`verdict_form_problems`, driven over synthetic drivers by tests/entities.py's `a driver printing no failing-check form the rule reads is reported`) -- never special-cased in the populator.
